reference: Scenario corpus for the Deviation / Clarification Register (technical queries, deviations, concessions) written from the public spec SPEC-deviationregister rev 2026-09-22.1 and the ISO 9000:2015 / ISO 9001:2015 clauses it cites (3.12.5 concession, 3.12.6 deviation permit, 3.1.5 configuration authority, 9001 8.3.6, 8.7.1 d, 8.7.2), plus TZ-project-package 2.3/3.4 for id, cross-reference, flag and conflict rules. It covers the five spec presets as headline cases, a trigger and a near-miss for each of the 34 rule ids, the authority-matrix fallback (exact-class rows replace '*' rows), the strict ageing boundary (age = target does not fire), bucket boundaries for default and custom edges, calendar arithmetic across a leap day, verdict ordering (empty before clear, 070 keeps an empty register out of 'empty'), the save gate, and the 4.6 metrics. Day counts and means are computed independently by deviationregister-ref.py (stdlib datetime ordinals); every hand-written hit set is re-checked by an independent evaluator of spec 3-6 in the same script.
reference_citations: ISO 9000:2015 Quality management systems - Fundamentals and vocabulary, 3.12.5 concession, 3.12.6 deviation permit, 3.6.4 requirement, 3.6.9 nonconformity, 3.1.5 configuration authority; definitions as reproduced in ISO/TC 176/SC 1 'Terms and definitions of ISO/TC 176 standards, alphabetical listing V1 2022-09-29', https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176sc1/files/Terms%20in%20TC%20176%20Standards%20Alphabetical%20Listing%20V1%202022%2009%2029.pdf

ISO 9001:2015 Quality management systems - Requirements, 8.3.6 design and development changes; 8.7.1 d) acceptance under concession; 8.7.2 c), d) documented information on concessions and the deciding authority (clause text as quoted in the spec source table S5-S7)

Proleptic Gregorian calendar day numbers: Python datetime.date.toordinal (deviationregister-ref.py)
tolerance: Categorical outcomes (verdict, rule presence/absence as (rule, target) pairs, save_allowed) exact. Severity counts, ages, buckets, response/disposition day counts, maxima and tallies are integers from integer calendar-day differences: exact. Means are arithmetic means of at most 7 integers: rel 1e-12, the float summation error bound for that operation; the spec's own grading (13) is looser (abs 0.0005 d) and any value passing this corpus passes it. A metric expected null must be null.
not_benchmarked: Engineering acceptability of a deviation or concession; adequacy of a user's authority matrix (spec 14).

Package runtime cases (explicit Load, conflict rows keep mine / take package, round trip of written deviations, ignored list, storage failure, atomic refusal on a real package document): interactive or runtime-level, covered by package QA per TZ-project-package 7.

Settings fallback value after an invalid entry ('previous valid value stays in force', 3.2): a corpus state has no previous value, so settings cases grade DEV-R-009 only and keep items whose outcome does not depend on the fallback.
The 'points at' field of each hit and the order of 'first offending date field' for DEV-R-003: only (rule, target) is graded, as spec 13 states.
Messages, next actions, localisation, report, figure, permalink, Python export self-test (spec 14).

Bid-evaluation field names beyond spec 7.2/7.4 (selected_bidder_id, compliance[].bidder_id, deviation_accepted) until reconciled with the bidevaluation spec; cases 070/072/073 use the names as stated.
coverage: 108 cases, 764 stated checks. Every one of the 34 rule ids has at least one triggering case and at least one case that asserts its absence (near-miss). Headline: presets P1-P5 with full hit sets, counts, verdicts and metrics as listed in spec 9. Boundaries: age = target / target+1 (acceptance 4), bucket ages 0,7,8,14,15,30,31 (acceptance 4), single, custom and default edges, settings limits 1/365/3650/5 entries, dates equal to as_of, leap day, empty raised_on sorting, equal-date tie-break by id. Acceptance 5 (exact row replaces '*'; '*' fallback; no row -> 012 alone), 6 (withdrawn/undecided not authority-checked), 7 (save gate for 001/002 only). Ten cases added by adjudication pass 1 (2026-09-23) close the holes listed in correction_notes; six added by adjudication pass 2 close the remaining ones: the invalid and after-as_of limbs of DEV-R-003 on responded_on, dispositioned_on and closed_on and the negative days(raised_on, dispositioned_on), the DEV-R-009 path settings.response_target_days.concession, DEV-R-014 raised by permitted_roles alone, DEV-R-050 on a concession, the DEV-R-060 tie-break where equal raised_on dates leave the larger id by string order as the later item, and a one-edge bucket key set. Disputable marks are resolved; no case was found wrong.
correction_notes: Adjudication 2026-09-23. All 92 original cases and their 592 checks were recomputed from the spec by an implementation written for this adjudication, independent of both the tool and the corpus author's reference script: 0 mismatches. The tool was re-run over the same 92 cases in Chromium through window.__dgcEvaluate: 0 failing checks, confirming the builder's zero as a measurement. No case was found wrong and none was removed.

Coverage holes closed by ten cases marked 'added by adjudication': approval-date-after-as-of and approval-date-invalid (the approvals[].date limb of DEV-R-003, previously unexercised); bid-evaluation-other-package (the bid-evaluation limb of DEV-R-056, only the vendor-document limb was covered); closed-without-closed-on (the 'status closed with empty closed_on' limb of DEV-R-004); duplicate-different-package (DEV-R-060 near-miss on package_id); bid-coverage-other-evaluation (register_covers requires the same bid_evaluation_id); concession-response-target (DEV-R-040/042 with a concession target set and the TQ target null); response-disposition-statistics-per-kind (the per-kind 4.6 statistics that no case graded); duplicate-id-both-items-counted and approval-role-merged-invalid-date (the two rulings of the spec changelog).

Two cases carried disputable: true. Both are resolved by the spec changelog of 2026-09-23 in the direction the corpus and the tool already took, so both cases stand unchanged with disputable set to false: unknown-approval-role (an unknown role is unpermitted, 011 beside 013) and duplicate-empty-package (package_id is compared as a string, so empty equals empty).

A differential sweep of 400 randomly generated states compared the tool with the independent implementation over verdict, hit set, counts, save_allowed and every metric: 0 differences after the two rulings above were applied. The sweep is the evidence that the coverage claim above is not merely self-consistent.

Adjudication 2026-09-23, pass 2. All 102 cases and their 705 checks were recomputed by a second independent implementation of spec 3-6, written for this pass from the spec text without reading src/rules.js, the tool's adapter or the corpus author's script: 0 mismatches. The tool was re-run over the same 102 cases in Chromium through window.__dgcEvaluate and graded outside the page: 705 of 705 checks pass, 0 page errors, 0 console errors.

A differential sweep of 1600 further states (900 adversarial: malformed ids and dates, 2026-02-29, month 13, settings outside every 3.2 limit in 664 of them, duplicate approval roles in 363 with an unorderable date in 77, duplicate item ids in 63, each context list absent in 218 to 507; 700 well-formed so that minor and info rules and the clear verdict dominate) compared the tool with that implementation on verdict, hit set as (rule, target) pairs, the four counts, save_allowed and every 4.6 metric: 0 differences. Across all 1708 states the tool emitted 34 distinct rule ids, none outside spec 5, and every hit carried the severity of the spec 5 column.

Six cases added by pass 2, marked 'added by adjudication (pass 2)', each reference hand-derived from the spec and then confirmed by the independent implementation: date-limbs-of-003, settings-concession-target-out-of-range, matrix-row-unknown-permitted-role, concession-without-requirement, duplicate-equal-dates-id-tiebreak, bucket-single-edge. The tool answers all 59 of their checks as stated.

The check id grammar is now written out in check_id_grammar. Four hit ids added by pass 1 omit the target altogether, which spec 13 allows; the page's benchmark adapter split them on a colon that is not there, truncating the rule id, and answered false against a rule that does not exist. All four carry ref false, so each passed on two falses meeting. The defect is the tool's, was found and fixed by the bench pass of 2026-09-23 (src/boot.js answerCheck), and the four ids are kept as written because they are the only cases that exercise the form.

check_id_grammar: Each case states its graded checks as a dict of check id -> {ref, tol, basis, derivation}. The ids are: 'verdict'; 'counts'; 'save_allowed'; 'metrics.<dotted path into the 4.6 metrics object>'; and 'hit:<rule id>[:<target>]'. A hit id with a target asks whether that (rule, target) pair is present. A hit id whose target is the single character '*', and a hit id with no target at all, both ask whether the rule fires on any target, which is the reading spec 13 gives an omitted target for presence and, negated, for absence. Both forms occur in this file: 220 hit ids name a target, 4 name none and 30 use '*'. A harness must split the rule id from the target on the FIRST colon after 'hit:' and treat its absence as '*'; splitting on a colon that is not there truncates the rule id and answers a check the corpus never stated.
